basis: BBS phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; cognitive impairment ~60% across BBS. Renal disease (~50%) omitted at cap; subtype-specific frequencies remain uncertain.

decisions.renal: none at cap: renal disease affects ~50% across BBS; cognitive impairment is more frequent. LZTFL1-specific frequencies are uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: involved: cognitive impairment is a major BBS feature, affecting ~60% overall; extrapolation to this sparsely described subtype warrants medium confidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: polydactyly is a major defining feature of the Bardet-Biedl phenotype represented by this concept.

basis: BBS phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity and polydactyly; cognitive impairment ~60% across BBS. Renal disease (~50%) omitted at cap; BBS5-specific frequencies remain uncertain.

decisions.renal: none at cap: renal disease affects ~50% across BBS; cognitive impairment is more frequent. BBS5-specific frequencies are uncertain.
decisions.neurologic: involved: cognitive impairment is a major BBS feature, affecting ~60% overall; subtype-specific frequency uncertainty limits confidence.

basis: Cardiac defects and skeletal abnormalities define Noonan syndrome; intellectual disability 5/5 defines this subtype. Strabismus 3/5; esophageal anomalies 2/5 omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability in 5/5 establishes neurodevelopmental impairment as a principal feature of BRAF-related Noonan syndrome.

basis: Structural skeletal myopathy. Respiratory failure and dysphagia occur in 30-79% but reflect respiratory and swallowing muscle weakness, without direct lung, gut or nerve damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory failure in 30-79% results from skeletal respiratory muscle weakness; direct pulmonary disease is not established.

basis: Intestinal lymph leakage causes enteropathy and immunodeficiency (80-99%); direct lymphocyte depletion occurs in 30-79%, with anemia reported in 80-99%.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: combined immunodeficiency is reported in 80-99%; the instructions require the mechanism axis whenever immunodeficiency applies.

basis: Branched-chain amino acid metabolic defect; headache, mild memory complaints and reflex signs in 1/1 do not establish lasting neurologic damage. Isolated ALT elevation does not establish liver injury.

decisions.neurologic: none: headache, mild memory complaints and reflex signs in one reported patient do not establish persistent direct neurologic injury or a typical damaging course.

basis: Infection-associated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS. Endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis are defining; neurologic injury occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: direct capillary endothelial injury and microvascular thrombosis define the thrombotic microangiopathy, meeting the diagnostic-feature exception.

basis: Lymphatic malformation and protein-losing enteropathy (2/2) define the phenotype; strabismus occurs in 2/2. Pneumothorax in 1/2 does not establish intrinsic pulmonary involvement.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pneumothorax in 1/2 is an isolated, separately diagnosed complication; direct pulmonary lymphatic disease is not established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal lymphangiectasia with protein-losing enteropathy is a defining Hennekam feature and is documented in 2/2 patients.

basis: Disease of the hypothalamus, a brain structure and hormone-secreting neuroendocrine organ; the definition includes neuroendocrine dysfunction. No additional organ damage is consistently established.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the hypothalamus is hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tissue, and neuroendocrine dysfunction is explicitly included in the disease definition.

basis: Inherited obesity-metabolic syndrome with defining hypertension in 26/35 (~74%). Coronary atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction are separately diagnosed sequelae.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is a core metabolic-syndrome feature and occurs in 26/35 (~74%); coronary disease and infarction are separate sequelae.
